claim: Start() implementations SHOULD enumerate all currently known endpoints via notifier.Upsert before entering the watch loop, to avoid serving an empty datastore at startup; implementations with a guaranteed-no-missed-events watch mechanism (e.g. a Kubernetes list+watch) MAY instead fold the initial enumeration into the watch sequence.
stance_target: startup-ordering requirement a custom discovery plugin must satisfy to avoid the router serving with zero known endpoints
quoted_support: Implementations SHOULD enumerate all currently known endpoints via notifier.Upsert before entering the watch loop, to avoid serving an empty datastore at startup. Implementations that guarantee no missed events through their watch mechanism (e.g. a Kubernetes list+watch) may fold the initial enumeration into the watch sequence instead.

claim: Ready()'s returned channel is closed at most once per Start invocation, only after a successful initial sync; if Start returns an error before that point the channel remains open, and 'zero endpoints is a valid outcome' for what counts as a completed initial sync.
stance_target: exact readiness-gating contract a custom discovery plugin must honor
quoted_support: The channel is closed at most once per Start invocation. It is closed only after a successful initial sync. If Start returns an error before that point, the channel remains open and callers waiting on it should also observe ctx cancellation... Zero endpoints is a valid outcome.

claim: DiscoveryNotifier is explicitly documented as NOT goroutine-safe: 'All calls must be made sequentially from a single goroutine,' with a strict ordering contract that the datastore processes Upsert/Delete in receipt order, and a same-endpoint Upsert-then-Delete sequence must preserve that order or the endpoint will be incorrectly left in the datastore.
stance_target: concurrency contract a custom discovery plugin must respect when emitting endpoint change events, a common source of subtle bugs for a new non-Kubernetes backend implementation
quoted_support: DiscoveryNotifier is NOT goroutine-safe. All calls must be made sequentially from a single goroutine... an Upsert followed by a Delete for the same endpoint must arrive in that order, or the endpoint will be incorrectly left in the datastore.

claim: A narrow adapter interface DiscoveryEndpointStore (methods EndpointUpsert(ctx context.Context, meta *EndpointMetadata) and EndpointDelete(id types.NamespacedName)) plus a NewDiscoveryNotifier(store DiscoveryEndpointStore) DiscoveryNotifier constructor exist in the same file, letting any conforming datastore be wrapped as a DiscoveryNotifier without a custom plugin re-implementing the notifier plumbing.
stance_target: the codebase already provides reusable scaffolding for wiring a new discovery source into the existing datastore, lowering the implementation burden for a custom non-k8s backend
quoted_support: DiscoveryEndpointStore is the narrow interface required by NewDiscoveryNotifier. Any store that implements EndpointUpsert and EndpointDelete satisfies it... NewDiscoveryNotifier wraps a DiscoveryEndpointStore as a DiscoveryNotifier.

claim: EndpointDiscovery embeds fwkplugin.Plugin (imported from github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/pkg/epp/framework/interface/plugin), meaning any custom discovery implementation must also satisfy whatever base Plugin interface that package defines, in addition to Start/Ready.
stance_target: full set of interfaces a custom discovery backend must implement, not just the two discovery-specific methods
